details: provides sentiment and intent analysis to an array of companies using SaaS and cloud based technology. Salience 6, the engine behind Lexalytics, was built as an on-premises, multi-lingual text analysis engine. It is leased to other companies who use it to power filtering and reputation management programs. In July, 2015 Lexalytics acquired Semantria to be used as a cloud option for its technology. In September, 2021 Lexalytics was acquired by CX company InMoment.

explainer.lead: Lexalytics is a company whose text-analysis engines provide sentiment and intent analysis to other businesses via on-premises and cloud software. It matters as an example of leased NLP infrastructure powering filtering and reputation management for client companies.

tiers.eli5: It is like a factory that builds a machine for reading customer opinions, then rents that machine to many companies instead of selling it outright.
tiers.practitioner: Companies lease the Salience engine for on-premises multilingual text analysis or use the Semantria cloud option to add sentiment and intent scoring to their own products. A consideration is deployment choice: on-premises versus cloud affects control over data and integration effort.
tiers.paperLevel: The company's engines are described as on-premises, multilingual text-analysis software leased to other firms; no algorithmic formulation is specified. Performance claims are not quantified here.

explainer.example: A reputation management vendor leases the Salience engine to score customer reviews for sentiment and route negative ones for follow-up.
